solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Talk about a long story

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the word for talk is read from its end

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to discuss a lengthy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk about' reads naturally as one phrase meaning discuss, but 'about' turns the word for talk round on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long, rambling account, originally a Norse epic tale of heroes.

clue.text: Good performer's excellent service

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an expert, a star at something
second meaning: in tennis, a serve the receiver cannot touch

explanation.surface: A fine player has a great serve.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a highly skilled person and an unreturnable serve in tennis.

clue.text: Side with a band that's heard

indicators.note: heard means we go by what is spoken, not how it is written

parts.note: a line is a band or stripe

explanation.surface: Join a group whose music is listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, but here it is a stripe, a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To align yourself with someone is to take their side or ally with them.

clue.text: European gripped by bad splenetic disease

indicators.note: something gripped is held inside, so this letter sits within the others
bad suggests something spoiled and out of order, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A foreigner is caught by a nasty, bad-tempered illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilence is a deadly epidemic disease, such as plague.

clue.text: Chap with letters after name welcoming graduate

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar
MA is a Master of Arts
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A man with qualifications after his name has a graduate degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters after name' looks like a list of degrees, but the definition is the chap with letters, a deliverer of mail; 'after' and 'name' are wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A postman is a man who delivers letters, a playful reading of a man with letters.

clue.text: Position that Oscar holds? Deputy

definitions.meaning: first meaning, cryptic: O, Oscar in the radio alphabet, is the second letter in the word command
second meaning: the officer next in rank below the leader

explanation.surface: Asks what rank a man named Oscar holds: deputy.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet, and O stands second in 'command'.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-in-command is the deputy who takes over when the leader is absent.

clue.text: Those who press to see the Queen in restraints

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other, like a prisoner in chains

parts.note: irons are shackles or fetters
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Journalists crowd round to see the monarch in chains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' suggests reporters, but it means pressing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironers are people who press laundry flat with an iron.

clue.text: African playing the piano all round India

indicators.note: all round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the extra one
playing suggests a performance that moves things about, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
India is I in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A musician from Africa tours India playing piano.
explanation.walkthrough: THE PIANO rearranged to ETHOPIAN, with I placed inside after ETH.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ethiopian is a person from Ethiopia, a country in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Kind of second-rate pants one must wear

indicators.note: wearing something puts it around you, so the letters enclose the extra one
pants is British slang for rubbish, so those letters are treated as junk to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Some sort of cheap underwear that a person has to put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' looks like 'a sort of', but Kind alone is the definition; 'pants' (British for rubbish, also underwear) is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A considerate person is kind, thoughtful about the feelings of others.

clue.text: Negligent first couple of reports by teacher

indicators.note: first couple of means take only the opening two letters

parts.note: the opening two letters of reports
pupils address a female teacher as Miss

explanation.surface: A slack teacher writes careless school reports.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means careless in carrying out one's duty.

clue.text: Idiot husband wearing golf trousers?

parts.note: a clot is a fool
H is the abbreviation for husband
someone in a coat is wearing it
G is golf in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A foolish husband dresses in golf trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that trousers are only one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers are an example of clothing, the garments people wear.

clue.text: A child star upset with all in chorus?

parts.note: taken as written
a son is a child

indicators.note: upset in a down light means turned upside down, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: a big name is a star

explanation.surface: A child celebrity is upset at being one of the chorus line.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as one man is to act together in unison, like voices in a chorus.

clue.text: One likely to snap at those driving over limit

definitions.text: One likely to snap at those driving over limit

parts.words: One likely to snap at those driving over limit
parts.note: surface reading: an angry person barking at drunk drivers
setter's reading: snap means photograph, and the limit is the speed limit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Over limit' suggests drink-driving and 'snap' suggests losing one's temper; both are misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: This roadside device photographs vehicles exceeding the posted speed limit.

clue.text: Strange old jerk pursuing old flame

indicators.note: pursuing means chasing behind, so these words are placed after the one they follow

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
O is the abbreviation for old
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: A weird former boyfriend chases his ex.
explanation.walkthrough: Old is used twice: once alone as an abbreviation, once inside 'old flame', a former lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic means strikingly unusual or foreign, so strange.

clue.text: Awfully indecent and best-limited inclinations

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: limited means losing its limits, so only the inner part of the word is kept

parts.note: the inner two letters of best

explanation.surface: Someone's dirty, barely restrained urges.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendencies are leanings or inclinations towards particular behaviour.

clue.text: Child host ordered to become washing-up helper?

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A party host makes a child help with the dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishcloth is a cloth used when washing up crockery, so it assists the washer.

clue.text: Couple I encountered from the East?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in an across light, coming from the east means travelling right to left, backwards

parts.note: met means encountered

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a pair they met from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a couple in a romantic relationship, as in 'they are an item'.

clue.text: Chances of dying do soar at the front

indicators.note: at the front means taking the leading letter of each word

parts.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: The risk of death climbs sharply on the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds are the likelihood or probability of something happening.

clue.text: European dominance upset grasping American leader

indicators.note: grasping means holding inside, so the rearranged letters enclose the extra one
upset means knocked into disorder, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: 'leader' keeps only the first letter of 'American'

parts.note: the leading letter of American

explanation.surface: A European power's supremacy is overturned while it holds a US president.
explanation.definitionFit: A Macedonian is a native of North Macedonia, a Balkan country in Europe.

clue.text: Cocktail party at centre held by midget

indicators.note: held by means placed inside, so these letters sit within the other word

parts.note: mini means very small, a midget size

indicators.note: at centre means taking only the middle letters of the word

parts.note: the middle three letters of party

explanation.surface: A tiny guest holds a cocktail at the heart of a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party at centre' asks for the middle of the word party, not a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: Showcase sample of pop in Underworld song

indicators.note: in places this letter inside the other words

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself

indicators.note: a sample is just a taste, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of pop
a lay is a short song or ballad

explanation.surface: A pop sample is showcased in a song by the band Underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld' looks like the dance act; here it is Dis, god of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To showcase something is to display it, putting it on show.

clue.text: Relish October's final on which the cup rests

parts.note: a relish is a sauce or condiment

indicators.note: final means taking only the last letter of the word

parts.note: the last letter of October

explanation.surface: A football fan relishes the October final where the trophy is up for grabs.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucer is the small dish on which a teacup sits.

clue.text: Investment minister has secured in error

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: Min is the abbreviation for minister
a stake is an investment in a venture

explanation.surface: A government minister wrongly obtains an investment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistaken means wrong, so someone in error is mistaken.

clue.text: Rhubarb served up following a cold ham

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: served up in a down light means placed upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: rhubarb is slang for nonsense, rot

explanation.surface: Rhubarb is served after cold ham in a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The menu surface hides two senses: rhubarb as nonsense and ham as a poor performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is an actor who overacts, so it stands for an actor.

clue.text: Miss when in Madrid, part of Essen, or Italy

indicators.note: part of means the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: run through the end of Essen, the word or, and the start of Italy

explanation.surface: A tourist is missed in Madrid, in Germany or Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Señorita is the Spanish title for an unmarried woman, the equivalent of Miss.

clue.text: Release hawk on Lahore's outskirts

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the outer letters of Lahore
to hawk goods is to tout them

explanation.surface: A falcon is freed on the edge of the Pakistani city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' looks like the bird but is the verb, to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: To let out is to release or set free.

clue.text: Do drugs lead to untold sadness and woe ultimately?

indicators.note: the lead is the front, so the first letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of untold

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letters are taken

parts.note: the last letter of sadness
the last letter of woe

explanation.surface: A warning: does taking drugs bring endless misery?
explanation.definitionFit: To use is slang for taking illegal drugs habitually.

clue.text: When one might suffer an awful shock?

definitions.text: When one might suffer an awful shock?

parts.words: When one might suffer an awful shock?
parts.note: surface reading: a moment of terrible fright
setter's reading: a shock is a mass of hair, here an unruly one

explanation.walkthrough: A shock of hair is a thick tangled mass, so an awful shock is untamed hair.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom describes a day when your hair will not behave, and by extension one where everything goes wrong.

clue.text: Instrument animal knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over means toppled, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a deer is an animal

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is toppled by a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a wind instrument, or the vibrating part of one, such as in an oboe.
